result.rationale: Verifiable from the diff: in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts the keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the string "[object Object]", so minimumTokenResponseSchema only requires access_token; zod strips unknown fields, and the code then sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`, overwriting the real token with a placeholder. In credential-sync mode (office365 CalendarService, salesforce) the persisted credential loses expiry/instance_url fields and gets a placeholder refresh_token. Real defect introduced by this diff.

judged_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:10 — both computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` become the same key "[object Object]", so minimumTokenResponseSchema is effectively `{access_token}`, and zod's default strip drops every other field (expires_in, expiry_date, instance_url, refresh_token). In sync mode the rows written by office365calendar (:264) and salesforce (CalendarService.ts:98) lose their real expiry and instance_url fields, and office365 also gets the placeholder refresh_token. (P1, conf 75)
